resources.string: Fixes exposure, colour and detail in your photos while keeping them true to the scene. Photos are processed on this phone and never uploaded.
Edits are saved automatically. Removing a project never deletes your photo.

Pixels edits photos on your phone. The app has no internet permission, so it cannot send your photos, edits or any other data anywhere.

What the app reads: only the photos you choose in the system photo picker. It reads the photo's pixels and its orientation tag. When you export with "Keep all" or "Remove location" metadata, it also reads the original's camera details (date, camera model, lens and exposure settings), and with "Keep all" its location, to copy them into the new file.

What the app stores: exported photos go to Pictures/Pixels in your gallery. Projects (your slider settings, crop and edit history, plus a reference to the original photo and a small preview image) are kept in the app's private storage. A temporary copy is made in the app's cache only when you use Share. Your last enhancement strength and export choices are remembered.

What the app does not do: no accounts, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking, no crash reporting, no cloud processing and no sharing with third parties.

Deleting your data: remove a project from Recent edits to delete its settings and preview. Exported photos are ordinary gallery files you can delete there. Clearing the app's storage or uninstalling removes all projects. Your original photos are never modified or deleted by the app.

If a future version adds any online feature, it will be opt-in and explained before anything leaves your device.

Pixels is provided free of charge, as is, without warranty of any kind. Automatic corrections are suggestions; review results before you rely on them.

You are responsible for having the right to edit and share the photos you open. Pixels never overwrites your originals, but keep your own backups of photos that matter.

The app adjusts the pixels that are already in a photo. It does not generate, add or remove people, objects or scenery, and it cannot recover detail the camera did not capture.

To the extent the law allows, the authors are not liable for any loss or damage arising from use of the app.

Pixels is built with Kotlin, kotlinx.coroutines and kotlinx.serialization (JetBrains) and Android Jetpack libraries including Compose, Activity, Lifecycle, Core and ExifInterface (Google), all under the Apache License 2.0. Image processing is Pixels\' own code.

Work from big to small: crop and level first, then light, then colour, then local fixes.

Open a photo, take one with the camera, or share one to Pixels from another app. Press and hold the photo to see the original. Drag anywhere along a slider to change it a little at a time, and double-tap a slider to reset it. Every finished change is one step in History. A dot under a tool means you changed something there.

Tap a preset, then set its Amount (0 to 200%). Save your own look with More, Save as preset; long-press one of yours to delete it. Auto fixes exposure, colour and noise; lower Auto strength for a lighter touch, or pick the right scene if it guessed wrong. Smart edit finds the subject, sky and background and edits each on its own; the result is three masks in Masking you can change.

Exposure moves everything; Highlights and Shadows recover bright and dark areas; Whites and Blacks set the end points. Show clipping marks pure white in red and pure black in blue. Curve: tap to add a point, drag it, double-tap it to remove.

White balance: Auto corrects colour casts, As shot keeps the camera\'s colours, and Pick white balance lets you tap something that should be grey or white. Vibrance boosts dull colours and spares skin. Mixer changes one colour at a time. Grading tints shadows, midtones and highlights. Calibration re-tunes all reds, greens and blues at once. Black and white uses the Mixer luminance sliders to set how light each colour turns out.

Texture and Clarity add or soften detail, Dehaze cuts haze. Vignette and Grain have shape controls for a film look. Sharpening Masking keeps skies and skin smooth; Colour noise reduction removes coloured speckles in night photos.

Crop, Auto levels the horizon. Optics fixes lens bulge, colour fringes, dark corners and purple or green fringing along edges. Geometry, Auto upright straightens leaning buildings; fine-tune with Vertical and Horizontal. The photo zooms just enough to hide empty edges.

Add a Subject, Sky or Background mask (found in the photo), a Brush, Linear or Radial gradient, Luminance range or Colour range mask. Turn on Show mask to see it in red. Paint and Erase work on any mask; Invert swaps inside and outside. Each mask has its own light and colour sliders.
Tap a blemish to remove it. Drag the dashed circle to choose another source. Clone copies exactly, for patterns and hard edges. Red eye: tap each red pupil; only strongly red pixels change.

Save writes a new file to Pictures/Pixels; your original is never changed. Choose JPEG, PNG or WebP, the size, what metadata to keep, and an optional border or watermark. History lists every change and named versions. Copy settings on one photo and Paste them on another, or use Apply to other photos to save many at once. Settings holds your defaults and storage controls.
Choose what to copy. Crop, masks and healing stay with this photo. Each photo is saved as a new file with your export settings; originals are not changed.
